summary: Intermittent elevated 5xx during large embedding upload: ephemeral-proxy accept-queue jam and upstream runtime disconnects
summary_timeline: 2026-03-13 14:05 UTC - First customer report via support form; 14:12 UTC - Alerts: ingestion error rate spike on tenant ClarityAI; 14:18 UTC - SRE observed elevated 502/503 across us-west edge; 14:33 UTC - Reproduced locally with large multipart embedding upload; 15:10 UTC - Temporary rate-limit applied for tenant; 15:45 UTC - Team investigating proxy accept-queue and nvme latency correlation
description:
Issue summary: Multiple ClarityAI requests uploading large embedding batches (~120k tokens total, chunked) started seeing 5xx responses (502/503) from the Redwood API gateway in prod-us-west. Errors began as a spike and turned into sustained elevated error rate for ~30 minutes. Impact: Affected customer experienced failed embedding imports (bulk job failures) and SDK retries. Observed impact confined to ClarityAI tenant in us-west; other tenants unaffected.

Environment: prod (us-west), dedicated tenant cluster for ClarityAI, serving-runtime 2026-02-28 build, proxy revision 2026-03-10.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproducible recipe):
1) Use ClarityAI bulk-upload pattern: multipart POST /v1/embeddings/upload with 2500 items, 32MB total payload.
2) Parallelize with 8 concurrent streams from one client IP.
3) Run for 1 minute.

Observed behavior: Gateway returns 502 or 503 intermittently across retries; logs show upstream runtime disconnects and ephemeral-proxy accept-queue growth to >95% of configured queue length. NVMe latencies on the embed-shard nodes increased (P99 ~ 240ms) around same time. Serving runtime emitted watcher log 'evicting worker due to response timeout' repeatedly.

Logs / excerpts: (sanitized)
- apigw: "2026-03-13T14:17:24Z ERROR route=upload tenant=clarityai upstream=disconnect code=502 msg=upstream closed connection"
- proxy: "accept_queue_length=198/200; ephemerals_in_use=48; conn_drops=6"
- runtime: "watchdog: response_timeout pid=2334 model=clarity-embed-large-v2"
- nvme: "iowait_p99_ms=240; io_depth=32; queue_stalls=12"

Hypothesis: Large embedding upload pattern causes burst of many small-fanout requests to the embedding shard. Ephemeral proxy accept-queue fills, causing connection drops to upstream runtimes which are also experiencing elevated NVMe iowait due to concurrent checkpoint/GC or background compaction. The combined effect triggers API Gateway retries and a retry-amplification loop resulting in sustained 5xx.

Immediate mitigation applied: Applied tenant-level temporary concurrency cap (reduced parallel streams to 2) and outbound hedged-retry tuning for the upload route; cleared accept-queue by rotating a small set of ephemerals (rolling restart of ephemeral proxies handling the tenant). Customer notified with temporary workaround.

Open questions:
- What triggered NVMe latency spike at 14:15? Background compaction was scheduled at 14:10 on shard nodes (check scheduler).
- Why did accept-queue not shed earlier (load-shedding config)?
- Do serving-runtime timeouts need to be extended for large multipart embedding uploads?
investigation_notes: 14:20 UTC - SRE: accept-queue metric shows sustained >90% and conn_drop spikes correlated with embedding upload throughput.
14:25 UTC - Infra: nvme compaction job started at 14:10 on embed-shard-3; iowait P99 rose to 240ms by 14:14.
14:30 UTC - Eng: runtime logs indicate repeated worker eviction due to response timeouts; kernel fallback not observed.
14:40 UTC - Tested reducing client parallelism from 8->2: errors drop to baseline and queues drain within 20s.
14:55 UTC - Applied temporary route-level backpressure: ingress concurrent limit for /v1/embeddings/upload lowered to 4 for all tenants on us-west to reduce blast radius.
15:05 UTC - Confirmed no other tenants impacted; load spike isolated to ClarityAI; but accept-queue aging logic did not trigger fast-enough shedding on these ephemeral proxies.

actions_taken: Tenant concurrency cap applied for ClarityAI (immediate).
Route-level ingress limit lowered to 4 on us-west for /v1/embeddings/upload (temporary safety).
Emergency throttle/abort of background NVMe compaction on embed-shard-3 (reduced iowait).
Rolled ephemeral proxy restart to flush accept-queue and clear stuck connections.
Customer advised to retry bulk upload with fewer concurrent streams; provided best-practice doc link.
next_steps: ENG: PR to tune proxy shedding to trigger earlier (target threshold 75%) and add exponential backoff in accept-queue drain behavior. (owner: Diego)

INFRA: Add NVMe maintenance blackout for embed-shards during known high-throughput customer windows and improve compaction scheduling logic. (owner: Priya)
CS: Coordinate with ClarityAI to reschedule large imports until fixes roll out; capture their preferred maintenance windows. (owner: Aisha)
SRE: Add a composite alert that correlates accept-queue, nvme iowait, and upstream disconnects to catch this pattern earlier. (owner: Maya)
resolution: pending - temporary mitigations successful (tenant concurrency cap + compaction abort + proxy restart) and customer resumed operations. Root cause traces to compaction + proxy accept-queue behavior; permanent fixes planned per next_steps. Will update ticket with PR numbers and rollout ETA.
resolution_notes: Customer impact mitigated at 15:00 UTC via concurrency cap and proxy rotation.
No data loss observed; most failed uploads were retried successfully after mitigation.
Follow-up action required: schedule runtime timeout change and proxy shedding PR; target rollout in maintenance window next week.
Documented temporary workaround in support KB: 'Bulk embedding upload best practices' and linked to customer email thread.
